title: Bacteria Staining
author: Guillermo Fernández Rodríguez
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.8gshtwe

steps.title: Inoculate overnight culture
steps.instruction: Pick a single E.coli DH5α colony from an LB agar plate with a sterile pipette tip and inoculate into 10 mL LB broth; incubate overnight at 37 °C.

steps.title: First centrifugation and resuspend
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the overnight culture at 4000 rpm for 5 minutes, discard the supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 10 mL of 50 mM NaHCO₃‑Na₂CO₃ buffer, pH 9.6, by inverting the tube.

steps.title: Second centrifugation and resuspend
steps.instruction: Centrifuge again at 4000 rpm for 5 minutes, discard the supernatant, and resuspend the pellet in 8 mL of 50 mM NaHCO₃‑Na₂CO₃ buffer, pH 9.6, mixing by inversion.

steps.title: Adjust optical density
steps.instruction: Measure the absorbance at 600 nm; dilute the suspension with the same 50 mM NaHCO₃‑Na₂CO₃, pH 9.6 buffer until the OD₆₀₀ equals 1.0.

steps.title: Prepare serial dilutions
steps.instruction: Make the following dilutions of the OD‑adjusted culture in 50 mM NaHCO₃‑Na₂CO₃, pH 9.6 buffer: 1:5, 1:10, 1:30, 1:50, and 1:100.

steps.title: Plate samples and incubate
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL of each diluted sample to wells of a Nunc MaxiSorp 96‑well plate and incubate overnight at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash wells with PBS‑Tween
steps.instruction: Wash each well three times with 200 µL PBS containing 0.1 % Tween, pH 7.4, discarding the liquid after the final wash.

steps.title: Stain with crystal violet
steps.instruction: Add 150 µL crystal violet to each well and incubate for 15 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Final washes and air‑dry
steps.instruction: Wash wells four times with 250 µL distilled water, then allow the plate to air‑dry for 1 hour 30 minutes before counting colonies under a microscope.
